Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: landscape editorial concept illustration for a computer-vision researcher's publication card, 3:2 aspect ratio.
Primary request: illustrate MapPano3D, which joins local 3D reconstructions from panoramic street videos into a coherent urban scene using a 2D road map, without additional neural-network training.
Composition: one clear compact isometric urban block at a road intersection, with several modest buildings and trees represented partly as fine point clouds and partly as solid paper-like surfaces. A thin flat road-map sheet sits underneath the reconstructed streets, its forest-green road lines visibly aligned to the 3D streets above. A small panoramic image strip along the foreground connects visually to the scene through a few subtle terracotta route dots. Keep every element legible at thumbnail size, generous breathing room.
Style: polished restrained editorial illustration, softly shaded architectural miniature with delicate stippling and subtle paper grain; warm ivory #f7f5ee background, dark forest green #35664c, muted sage, terracotta #be654b accents. Academic, calm, human, consistent with a personal research notebook website.
Constraints: purely conceptual and not an experimental output; no plots, metrics, before/after claims, exact geographic map, labels, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, sci-fi holograms or decorative unrelated objects. No embedded title. Wide landscape canvas.

Illustrate geometric alignment of dental cone-beam CT and intraoral scans. A translucent pale gray-green dental volume containing anatomically plausible upper and lower dental arches with gray roots is the central subject. Slightly offset terracotta crown-surface meshes hover close to their matching teeth. Thin dotted green correspondence lines and one gentle curved arrow express moving these crown surfaces into alignment. Subtle colored thin bands on crown surfaces suggest the learned crown-support regions. Use a compact three-quarter view of both arches with a narrow gap between upper and lower teeth. Keep the roots gray and the gum-free crown shells terracotta so different inputs read clearly. No new complete tooth reconstruction: the concept is aligning existing surfaces. No opaque flesh, frightening skull, dental tools or more than one dominant visual grouping.

Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: a NEW landscape 3:2 editorial method illustration for an academic publication card. This must explain the contribution of the paper "High-Fidelity 3D Tooth Reconstruction by Fusing Intraoral Scans and CBCT Data via a Deep Implicit Representation", not merely show two tooth parts joining.

Scientific content: IOS supplies a detailed crown; CBCT supplies complete root geometry. After registration, these form a rough hybrid proxy with a visible seam and uneven surface. This proxy becomes a geometric fitting target for a PRETRAINED INCISOR DeepSDF shape prior. Optimizing the latent shape code z fits a continuous implicit surface to the target. The output is one smooth, closed, complete incisor. The network weights are fixed during this fitting; do not depict training the network on this example.

Composition: three clearly spaced regions, with the main visual emphasis on the CENTRAL fitting operation.
LEFT, about 25% of canvas: two small aligned input forms, a muted terracotta detailed incisor crown without a root and a sage-gray full CBCT incisor with root, feeding a slightly larger two-color hybrid tooth below them. Its crown-root junction has a small visibly irregular seam. Label the inputs "IOS" and "CBCT", and the combined form "Hybrid proxy".
CENTER, about 45% of canvas: a delicate translucent rounded rectangle contains a dashed/ghosted outline of the rough hybrid target overlaid with a smoothly continuous green implicit tooth surface. Several restrained nested signed-distance contours surround the tooth. A small curved optimization-loop arrow wraps around the latent fitting, labeled "Optimize latent code z". Above this panel place three SMALL faint incisor silhouettes representing the learned shape family, with a fine arrow into the fitting panel, labeled "Pretrained DeepSDF prior". The center must read as fitting a learned complete shape to scan evidence, not simple smoothing or direct stitching. An arrow comes in from the left hybrid proxy and another leaves toward the right final surface.
RIGHT, about 23% of canvas: a single beautiful continuous complete incisor rendered in UNIFORM warm ivory with subtle forest-green contour shading, no two-color crown-root split, no seam, no fake numerical results. Label "Complete surface".
No overall title, no extra labels, only these six short English labels exactly. Use spacious dark-green sans-serif text, readable at thumbnail size; avoid clutter or tiny type.

ANATOMY IS CRITICAL: every upright incisor has its broad, nearly straight cutting/incisal edge at the TOP, facing away from the root. Crown sides taper DOWN toward a narrower cervical neck. The single elongated root extends DOWN from that neck to a tapered apex. Never put the broad scalloped cutting edge at the crown-root junction. Match crown-neck and root widths. The crown is roughly one third to two fifths of the total tooth length; the root occupies the remaining length. Use incisors, no multi-root molars.
